questions.prompt: What is aimlessness in this law?
choices: A temporary lack of motivation after a setback
Movement without an organizing direction or mission
A refusal to work hard at all

explanation.gentle: The chapter defines aimlessness as drift, not simply laziness.
explanation.direct: The problem is activity without a governing purpose.
explanation.competitive: Motion keeps happening, but no strategy allocates it.

questions.prompt: Why does Greene use Martin Luther King Jr. in this chapter?
choices: To show a life whose force came from mission and direction
To argue that only public leaders can have real purpose
To prove that purpose removes fear and sacrifice

explanation.gentle: King anchors the law in a life organized by mission.
explanation.direct: The case shows how purpose gathers talent and urgency into directed force.

A path shaped mainly by prestige, pressure, or borrowed expectations
A quiet goal that requires patience

explanation.gentle: False purpose often looks admirable from the outside.

questions.prompt: A professional keeps saying yes to every exciting opportunity and cannot explain what larger direction any of it serves. Which reading best fits the chapter?
choices: The person is showing healthy flexibility
The person may be mistaking busyness for purpose
The person has already found the right mission

explanation.gentle: The warning sign is motion without clear direction.
explanation.direct: Too many yeses can signal weak mission rather than strength.
explanation.competitive: The portfolio is filling without a governing strategy.

questions.prompt: Which personal pattern most clearly shows a borrowed goal rather than real purpose?
choices: Someone keeps pursuing a path mainly because it looks impressive to others
Someone chooses a quieter path that still feels meaningful over time
Someone cuts one commitment to protect deeper work

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns that admiration from others can disguise weak fit.
explanation.direct: External approval can keep counterfeit purpose alive.
explanation.competitive: Prestige can keep drift looking legitimate.

questions.prompt: In the chapter's terms, what is one of the clearest signs that direction is weak?
choices: A packed schedule with no hierarchy for what matters most
A willingness to say no to some distractions
A mission that deepens over time

explanation.gentle: Scattered effort is a common sign of aimlessness.
explanation.direct: When every demand feels equally urgent, the mission is not filtering well.

questions.prompt: Why does purpose make discipline easier to sustain?
choices: Because it removes all uncertainty from life
Because it gives effort a clearer reason and filters distractions
Because it guarantees public recognition

explanation.gentle: Purpose helps effort feel more coherent.
explanation.direct: A real mission makes sacrifice easier to understand and defend.
explanation.competitive: Mission turns friction into legible cost.

questions.prompt: Why can busyness be misleading in this chapter?
choices: Because all hard work is secretly meaningless
Because activity can hide drift when no mission is organizing it
Because purpose always requires a slower life

explanation.gentle: The chapter warns against mistaking motion for direction.
explanation.direct: A full calendar can still belong to an aimless life.

questions.prompt: How does chapter 14 connect to chapter 13 on gender rigidity?
choices: Chapter 14 rejects the idea that identity affects direction
Chapter 14 asks where the wider range recovered in chapter 13 should actually be aimed
Chapter 14 proves identity no longer matters once purpose appears

explanation.gentle: Once the self regains range, the next question is what that range should serve.
explanation.direct: Chapter 13 recovers capacity; chapter 14 asks for direction.

questions.prompt: Which plan best fits the law of aimlessness?
choices: Say yes to every promising option until your purpose becomes obvious by accident
Identify the work that keeps recurring, cut one borrowed commitment, and organize your week around the stronger direction
Wait for one dramatic moment of certainty before changing anything

explanation.gentle: The chapter asks for chosen direction and gradual reorganization, not passivity.
explanation.direct: Purpose is built by filtering commitments and aligning effort, not by waiting for perfect clarity.
explanation.competitive: Reprice the week around mission instead of letting noise bid on every slot.
